doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sarah Vaughan as unaffected and sassy
summary: Sarah was sassy, unaffected, and sang Look to the Rainbow.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And we talked about Carmen, unless there‘s anything else.
And Sarah Vaughn we also talked about.

What did I say about . . . Sarah came and ate a half a meatloaf before the rest of the food was ready. She was a good girl, she‘s a good girl. And she was unaffected by the whole thing. You know, God gave her the most beautiful instrument in the world, and she was just sassy. It didn‘t mean anything. She just went on and did it. That was it, went on about her business, and let‘s party. She wasn‘t serious at all. Well, that‘s good, you know. I guess it‘s good to be that way, because you don‘t get gray hairs. She didn‘t worry about a damn thing. [laughs]
Sometime I asked about her husband, she said, ―What husband?‖ [laughs] And she had a couple of dogs, too. But she sang. She sang Look to the Rainbow. It makes me cry every time I hear it.
